item.title: Over 3,000 already dead from cholera this year, says WHO
item.description: Cholera has killed more than 3,000 people worldwide since the start of the year, the World Health Organization said on Tuesday, insisting its goal of cutting global cases by 90 percent by 2030 remained in reach. The disease killed nearly 7,900 people in 2025, making it “the deadliest year for cholera since 1999”, according to Lorenzo Pezzoli, WHO lead for epidemic-prone bacterial diseases. item.title: Hong Kong customs targets use of astronaut Yang Liwei’s name to sell ‘space oil’
item.description: Hong Kong customs has requested the removal of e-commerce and social media listings by drug dealers who used the name of Chinese astronaut Yang Liwei as a code name to push “space oil”, also known as etomidate. Yang’s name was just one example of the subtle linguistic workarounds used by illicit vendors to evade platform filters. Customs had made about 64 requests to remove illicit items from platforms including Taobao, JD.com and Pinduoduo since signing agreements with them over the past year,... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Un nuevo fármaco experimental para adelgazar se ha visto que también ayuda a aliviar el dolor de las rodillas con artrosis
item.description: La nueva generación de fármacos contra la obesidad está a la vuelta de la esquina con menos efectos secundarios y resultados más sorprendentes. Uno de los que está dando mejores sensaciones es la retatrutida, que es un compuesto experimental desarrollado por Eli Lilly y que actúa como un triple agonista hormonal. Pero la buena noticia es que sus efectos pueden ir más allá de la simple pérdida de peso. Bajo estudio. Los últimos estudios que se han publicado en torno a este fármaco provienen de dos grandes ensayos clínicos de fase 3, bautizados como TRIUMPH-4 y TRIUMPH-1-OA. En estos se tomaron… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: Tests on 8 frozen Inca mummies sacrificed show they had chewed coca leaves and had drunk alcohol
item.description: A remarkable archaeological find has revealed eight frozen mummies of children from the Inca Empire, believed to have been sacrificed. Analysis of their hair and nails showed they've ingested coca and alcohol, hinting at a diversity of ritual practices based on local customs. Notably, one mummy, Juanita, contained harmine traces, suggesting specialized ritualistic preparations. This research unveils a rich tapestry of ancient cultural traditions and ceremonies. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: In China’s fierce race for success, mental health struggles are starting earlier

Chen’s mother rushed her to a cardiologist – only to be told that she should see a psychiatrist instead.
